subject: Network boundary & control/data split — integration consensus and next steps
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: sarah.lin@arcadiahealth.com, ops@coloops.com
Date: 2026-08-26T09:12:00Z
Subject: Initial integration checks — control plane / data plane boundaries (attachments)

Hi all,

Thanks for coming together quickly. Attached are two artifacts I want the group to sanity-check before we lock the runbook for Arcadia's on‑prem deployment: 1) onprem-network-diagram-v3.pdf (logical overlay + demarc), and 2) controlplane-dataflow-table.xlsx (who owns what, ports, certs).

High-level ask: confirm the control-plane placement (centralized in Arcadia colo, routed across L3 peering) and the data-plane demarcation (tenant traffic terminates on their L3 edge, kept off our control plane network). Key open questions I noted: 
- Egress path for model telemetry (do we allow telemetry egress via Arcadia NAT or must it traverse Redwood egress gateway?)
- Crossconnect QoS: target RTT budget per inference hop (we proposed <10ms p50 intra-datacenter; confirm)
- Certificate rotation boundary (Arcadia KMS vs Redwood CA for node certs)

Please reply with line-by-line confirmations or small edits in the diagram; if anything needs rework, include a short rationale. If we can get consensus by EOD we can post the runbook and schedule a short cutover dry-run next week.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov

+1 415 555 0132

Date: 2026-08-26T10:02:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial integration checks — control plane / data plane boundaries (attachments)

Thanks Olga — quick acknowledgements below.

On Wed, Aug 26, 2026 at 09:12, Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com> wrote:
> High-level ask: confirm the control-plane placement (centralized in Arcadia colo...)

- Control plane placement: Arcadia is fine hosting the control plane in our primary colo (rack C12). We will provide BGP adjacency into Redwood's management VLAN.
- Telemetry egress: prefer that telemetry flow over Arcadia's egress (we have existing peering & inspection pipelines) — would like to avoid new outbound paths from our security team. If Redwood requires a specific egress IP range, please provide it.
- RTT budget: 10ms p50 looks reasonable inside the colo; cross-site links to DR site will be higher (~25ms). We need the plan to call out tolerant thresholds for cross-site failover.
- Cert rotation: Arcadia can run node certs via our internal KMS, but we need to see the CSR process and renewal timetable.

Two asks for the runbook: 1) include a short checklist for the colo ops (patching windows, BFD config), and 2) a table with expected firewall rules (we'll share our edge ACL template).

I'll loop internal ops on a separate thread with the ACL template.

— Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Infrastructure, Arcadia Health
sarah.lin@arcadiahealth.com
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-08-26T12:30:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial integration checks — control plane / data plane boundaries (attachments)

Uploading a few clarifications and a config snippet — see attached mplsl3 snippet.

A few notes: 
- Routing: we'll peer via a /30 between Redwood mgmt plane and Arcadia's BGP VLAN. We'll originate only management routes (no tenant CIDRs). Tenant routes will be learned via static or via Arcadia side L3.
- NAT / egress: given Arcadia's preference for telemetry egress, we'll mark telemetry flows with DSCP 0x2 and expect Arcadia to carry them through their inspection pipeline. If we detect repeated drops we'll provide fallback to Redwood egress via VPN tunnel.
- QoS: recommend EF for control-plane heartbeats and AF for telemetry; tenant inference flows stay best-effort.

Config snippet (attachment: mpls-l3edge-config-snippet.txt):
! ---- snippet start ----
interface Gig1/2
 description Redwood peering to Arcadia C12
 ip address 10.254.12.2 255.255.255.252
 ip router bgp 65110
  neighbor 10.254.12.1 remote-as 64521
! ---- snippet end ----

I'll add these into the runbook spreadsheet with exact ACL rows.

Jonas
Sr. Network Engineer, Redwood Inference
jonas_weber@redwood.com
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: olga@redwood.com, jonas_weber@redwood.com
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com, naomi_feldman@redwood.com, sarah.lin@arcadiahealth.com
Date: 2026-08-26T14:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial integration checks — control plane / data plane boundaries (attachments)

On Wed, Aug 26, 2026 at 12:30, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com> wrote:
> - Routing: we'll peer via a /30 between Redwood mgmt plane and Arcadia's BGP VLAN.

Couple of concerns from the control-plane perspective:
1) Telemetry integrity: If Arcadia terminates telemetry, we need guaranteed TLS termination details and an IP allowlist for our agents. Without that we can't ensure credentialed uploads (tokens are minted by our control plane).
2) Failover choreography: propose adding a short subroutine in the runbook: if the Arcadia egress path becomes unavailable, flip telemetry to the Redwood tunnel and increment a telemetry_failover counter (observability hook). We should record that event in the audit logs and surface it on the console.
3) Certificate lifecycle: recommend the runbook include a CSR template and a weekly rotation window (30m maintenance) to avoid surprises.

If Arcadia agrees to the telemetry handshake details (TLS endpoints, SNI, IPs), we'll finalize the control-plane steps. Otherwise we should plan a dry-run where telemetry is routed to Redwood for 24h to validate flows.

Karthik
Head of Platform Integrations, Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com
From: Olga Petrov <olga@redwood.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.com, karthik_iyer@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com

Date: 2026-08-26T16:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial integration checks — control plane / data plane boundaries (attachments)

Thanks everyone — summary and next steps below.

Summary of decisions: 
- Control plane: hosted in Arcadia colo (rack C12). Redwood mgmt VLAN via /30 BGP peering is accepted.
- Data plane: tenant traffic remains on Arcadia L3 edge; Redwood will not advertise tenant prefixes.
- Telemetry egress: primary = Arcadia egress (per Sarah). Fallback = Redwood tunnel. Karthik's request for TLS details and an IP allowlist is noted as an action item.
- Cert rotation: Arcadia will handle node certs; Redwood to publish CSR template and renewal window.

Action items (owners & due dates):
- Arcadia (Sarah): share ACL template + production egress IP range — due 2026-08-28.
- Jonas: paste final ACL rows and the BGP snippet into controlplane-dataflow-table.xlsx and mark done — due 2026-08-27. Attachment: mplsl3 config submitted.
- Karthik: draft telemetry fallback subroutine and audit-log hook (will add to runbook) — due 2026-08-30.
- Olga: schedule a 1.5h dry-run window (telemetry routed to Redwood) on 2026-09-02 and send calendar invite — scheduled when actions complete.

I'll produce an updated runbook (final v4) by EOD tomorrow incorporating these items and the ACL template when Sarah sends it. If there are any objections please flag them inline on the doc.

Olga
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
olga@redwood.com
